content.value_statement: Building LibreOffice Base databases can require many steps across tables, queries, forms, and reports. This skill guides structured database workflows and automation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Outlines ODB database creation workflows with command-line and UNO examples.
Shows connection string formats for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, ODBC, and JDBC data sources.
Provides Python UNO examples for Base document creation and MySQL connection setup.
Lists LibreOffice command-line options for Base and headless automation.
Summarizes database practices for indexes, transactions, backups, schema documentation, and data types.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or automated validation tools.
Uses placeholder file paths, hosts, ports, database names, and credentials.
Assumes LibreOffice, database drivers, and Python libraries are already installed.
Does not provide advanced database security hardening guidance.

use_cases.title: Create an Internal Database
use_cases.description: Plan tables, relationships, and an ODB file for a small operational database.

use_cases.title: Connect Existing Data Sources
use_cases.description: Use connection string references to connect Base with MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, ODBC, or JDBC sources.

use_cases.title: Automate Reports
use_cases.description: Use UNO and headless LibreOffice patterns to support repeatable database report workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Base Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a LibreOffice Base database for [purpose]. Include tables, key fields, relationships, and recommended data types.

prompt_templates.title: Build Connection Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Create setup guidance for connecting LibreOffice Base to [database type]. Include the connection string shape, required drivers, and common checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Forms and Reports
prompt_templates.prompt: Design forms and reports for a LibreOffice Base database with these tables: [tables]. Include data entry flow and report outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Base with UNO
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an automation plan for LibreOffice Base using Python UNO. Include startup mode, connection handling, document storage, and error handling.

output_examples.input: Plan a small inventory database in LibreOffice Base.
output_examples.output: A table plan with products, suppliers, stock movements, primary keys, foreign keys, and suggested forms for receiving and issuing stock.

output_examples.input: Connect LibreOffice Base to PostgreSQL for reporting.
output_examples.output: A concise setup checklist covering driver installation, connection string format, credential handling, test queries, and report validation.

output_examples.input: Create a monthly sales report workflow.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline covering source tables, saved queries, report layout, headless execution, export steps, and review checks.

best_practices: Use parameterized queries and transactions for database changes.
Document table relationships, connection settings, and report assumptions.
Back up ODB files and external databases before automation or schema changes.
anti_patterns: Do not store production passwords directly in shared examples or prompts.
Do not run headless automation against live databases without backups.
Do not mix placeholder connection strings with production credentials.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and automate LibreOffice Base databases, connections, forms, reports, and basic data workflows.

faq.question: Does it create a working ODB file automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that a user can adapt in their own LibreOffice environment.

faq.question: Which databases are covered?
faq.answer: The skill references embedded HSQLDB and Firebird, plus MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, ODBC, and JDBC sources.

faq.question: Can it help with Python UNO automation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes UNO patterns for connecting to LibreOffice and creating or storing Base documents.

faq.question: Does it handle credentials securely?
faq.answer: It uses placeholders and does not store real credentials. Users should keep secrets outside shared prompts and files.

faq.question: Is this skill suitable for production database operations?
faq.answer: It is a planning and reference aid. Production use needs backups, access controls, testing, and local security review.
